    LargeIndecomposable.AR.DirData.exists_brick_off

    Roots off a point are bricks #

    Let D be a directed algebra with a sincere directing module whose indecomposables killed by any e_i are rigid (RigidOff). A module of minimal endomorphism dimension with dimension vector x ≥ 0, x_a = 0, is rigid (rigid_of_minEnd), so dim End ≤ ⟨x, x⟩ (hom_le_euler). Hence a root off a point is the dimension vector of a module with one-dimensional endomorphism algebra (exists_brick_off).

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.AR.DirData.exists_brick_off {k A : Type u} [Field k] [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] {D : DirData k A} {U : FDMod k A} (hT : ∀ (x : D.ι), x ∈ D.T) (hU : Directing U) (hs : D.Sincere U) (hR : D.RigidOff) (a : D.ι) (x : D.ι → ℤ) (hx : Forms.UnitForm.Pos x) (hxa : x a = 0) (h1 : euler D x x = 1) :
    ∃ (V : FDMod k A), dimZ D V = x ∧ Module.finrank k (V.carrier →ₗ[A] V.carrier) = 1

    A root off a point is the dimension vector of a brick.
